```{r, Installing packages, include= FALSE}

library(tidyverse)
library(lme4)
library(mosaic)
library(xtable)
library(DescTools)
```

## Objective 1

```{r, data cleaning}
final <- read.csv("Data/final.csv") |> #Importing the data
  mutate(distance = sqrt((x-50)^2 + (y)^2)) |> #Creating the distance metric using the distance formula
  mutate(angle = acos(abs(x- 50) /distance)* 180/pi) #Creating the angle metric using the angle formula
final$outcome <- ifelse(final$outcome == "goal", TRUE, FALSE) #Set goals to binary true and false
```

#### Model

```{r, Model for regression}
fit = glmer(outcome~angle+distance +angle : distance + (1 + angle +distance + angle : distance | player), family = binomial, data = final ) #Creates our multiple linear regression line with a rank based for each player for angle distance and the interaction term as well. 
fit_long = fit # Set fit equal to fit long
summary(fit_long)$coef # show the coeficients of the models 
#ranef(fit_long)$player
#xtable( summary(fit_long)$coef, digits = 4 ) Creates the latex tables of the model
```

#### Graph for Specific Points

```{r, graphing_specfic points within the model}
#Goal is to show a distribution for every player as a point and how it can be modeled
new_data <- data.frame(
  angle = c(0, 50),
  distance = c(50, 0)
) # The points that we are testing at

predict(fit_long, newdata = new_data, type ="response", re.form = NA) #Predicts the outcomes

#pdf( "At_points.pdf", height = 5 * 0.9, width = 8 * 0.9 ) Creates the graphic

beta = as.numeric( summary(fit)$coef[,1] ) #sets beta 
b = ranef(fit)$player # b is the random effect per player

noah = 2 #Sets the random seed for adjustment

ang = 20; dis = 10 # Test point 1 
mu = ( beta[1] + b[,1] ) + ( beta[2] + b[,2] ) * ang + ( beta[3] + b[,3] ) * dis + ( beta[4] + b[,4] ) * ang * dis # enter it into the model
theta = exp(mu) / (1 + exp(mu)) #find theta
plot( density(theta, adjust = noah), type = "l", col = 1, lty = 1, xlim = c(0, 0.65), ylim = c(0, 11),  #Plot theta and make the first line on the graph
      xlab = "Predicted Probability", main = "", ylab = "", axes = FALSE )
axis( 1, seq( -0.2, 1, 0.2 ) )


ang = 0; dis = 15 # repeats the same steps for a second point
mu = ( beta[1] + b[,1] ) + ( beta[2] + b[,2] ) * ang + ( beta[3] + b[,3] ) * dis + ( beta[4] + b[,4] ) * ang * dis
theta = exp(mu) / (1 + exp(mu))
lines( density(theta, adjust = noah), col = 2, lty = 2 )

ang = 45; dis = 35 # repreats the steps again for a third point
mu = ( beta[1] + b[,1] ) + ( beta[2] + b[,2] ) * ang + ( beta[3] + b[,3] ) * dis + ( beta[4] + b[,4] ) * ang * dis
theta = exp(mu) / (1 + exp(mu))
lines( density(theta, adjust = noah), col = 4, lty = 4 )

legend("topright", legend = c("D = 10 A=20", "D = 15 A=0", "D = 35 A=45"), lty = c(1, 2, 4), col = c(1, 2, 4), bty = "n") #Creates a legend explaining each individual level

#dev.off()
```

#### Creating The Heatmap

```{r, heatmap}
grid <- expand.grid(
  x = 1:100,
  y = 1:100
) # Creates a 100 by 100 grid


grid <- grid |>
  mutate(d = sqrt((x-50)^2 + (y)^2)) |>
  mutate(a =acos(abs(x - 50) /d)* 180/pi)
#Finds each point on the grids angle and distance

grid$p <- predict(
  fit,
  newdata = data.frame(distance = grid$d, angle = grid$a),
  type = "response",
  re.form = NA
) # Finds the predicted probability at each point
grid <- grid |>
  mutate(d = sqrt((x-50)^2 + (y)^2)) |>
  mutate(a =acos(abs(x - 50) /d)* 180/pi) #Creates the grid Distance and angle so we are able to use the predict function

grid$p <- predict(
  fit,
  newdata = data.frame(distance = grid$d, angle = grid$a),
  type = "response",
  re.form = NA
) # creates the prediction at every distance and angle
#pdf( "2025_heatmap", height = 5, width = 7)
grid |>
  ggplot(aes(x=x, y=y, fill = p))+ #Specify what x and y is and fills it based on probability
  geom_raster()+ # Creates a heatmap
  scale_fill_viridis_c( option = "H", 
                        breaks = seq(min(grid$p),
                                     max(grid$p),
                                     length.out=10), # groups the probability scale by 10
                        labels = function(x) round(x, 2),
                        name = "Probability")+
  geom_contour(aes(z=p),colour = "white", bins = 10)+ #Creates the rings around each group
  geom_rect( xmin = 25, xmax = 75, ymin = 0, ymax = 25, colour = "yellow", #Creates the rectange of the penalty area
             fill = NA, linewidth = 1 )+
  annotate("text", x=50, y=79, color ="white", label = "0.08")+ #annotates each ring with the probability of that ring
  annotate("text", x=50, y=59, color ="white", label = "0.16")+
  annotate("text", x=50, y=48, color ="white", label = "0.24")+
  annotate("text", x=50, y=38, color ="white", label = "0.32")+
  annotate("text", x=50, y=30, color ="white", label = "0.4")+
  annotate("text", x=50, y=21, color ="white", label = "0.47+")

#dev.off() #Stops the pdf
```

#### Second Heatmap

```{r, heatmap_player}

)
```

#### Difference Heatmap

```{r, heatmap_diff}

grid_diff$p <- grid2$p -grid$p #Finds the difference between the probability of the player compared to the league average.

#tally(~grid_diff$p>0) Just checking the average difference for the player

grid_diff |> 
  ggplot(aes(x=x, y=y, fill = p))+ #Similar code to the other 2 heatmaps
  geom_raster()+

    xmin = 25, xmax = 75,
    ymin = 0, ymax = 25,
    colour = "yellow",
    fill = NA,
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  geom_contour(aes(z=p),colour = "white", bins = 5)
  
#dev.off()
```

## Objective 2

#### Model

```{r, objective_2_cleaning_model}
goalie_24 <-read.csv("Data/K1_24.csv") |> # Mutating the dataset for 2024 the same as 2025
  select(-X) |>
  mutate(distance = sqrt((x-50)^2 + (y)^2)) |>
  mutate(angle = acos(abs(x- 50) /distance)* 180/pi) 
goalie_24$outcome <- ifelse(goalie_24$outcome == "goal", TRUE, FALSE)
  

fit_24 = glmer(outcome~angle+distance +angle : distance + (1 + angle +distance + angle : distance | player), family = binomial, data = goalie_24  ) #Creating the same glmer except for the 2024 season
summary(fit_24)
```

#### 2024 Heatmap


#### More cleaning for objective 2

```{r, difference_cleaning}
final_25 <- final |> #Creating variable for year for 2025
  mutate( year = 25)


final_24 <- goalie_24 |> #Creating variable for year for 2024
  mutate(year = 24)

final_24_25 <- rbind(final_24, final_25) #Combining those 2 datasets
final_24_25 = as.data.frame(final_24_25)
#head(final_24_25)
#unique( final_24_25$player )
x <- intersect(final$player, goalie_24$player) #Finding the intersect of players who played both seasons
index = which( final_24_25$player %in% x ) #Saves the players who are in the intersect 
final_z = final_24_25[index,] #saves the players in the intersect

shot_pct_by_player <- final_z %>% #Simplifies the dataset
  group_by(player, year) %>%
  summarise(
    save_percentage = mean(outcome == "FALSE"),
    saves = count(outcome == "FALSE"), #Creates the saves variable
    attempts = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

shot_wide <- shot_pct_by_player |>
  mutate(year = trimws(as.character(year))) |> # TUrns the data wide instead of long that way we can compare between the 2 years
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = year,
    values_from = c(save_percentage,attempts, saves)
  )
shot_clean <- shot_wide |> #Cleans the data so we only have data from 2024 and 2025 for the variables we care about
  group_by(player) |>
  summarise(
    pct_24= max(save_percentage_24, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_25= max(save_percentage_25, na.rm = TRUE),
    saves_24,
    attempts_24,
    saves_25,
    attempts_25
    ) |>
  filter(player != "Kim Yu-Sung") #Removes this player as he only has one shot attempted on him and was scored on so he appears as a major outlier
```

#### Difference Graphs

```{r, Model_grahic_difference}
fit = glm( saves_25/attempts_25 ~ pct_24, data = shot_clean, family = binomial, 
           weights = attempts_25) #Creates our model between 2024 and 2025 the weights specifiy that the 2035 one is what it is in relation to. As the attempts the goalkeeper faces is important.
summary(fit)

shot_clean$pred <- predict(fit, type = "response") #Creates a prediction line


#pdf( "24_25.pdf", height = 5, width = 8) Allows us to save the graph

ggplot(aes(x = pct_24, y = pct_25), data=shot_clean)+ #Creates a graph 
  geom_point()+
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "red")+
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.6,0.8), ylim =c(0.6,0.8))+
  geom_line(aes(y=pred), color = "blue")+
  labs(x = "Proportion of shots saved in 2024",
       y ="Proportion of shots saved in 2025")

#dev.off() Turns off the graph

cor.test( pct_25 ~ pct_24, data = shot_clean )
```

## Objective 3

```{r, shot proportion when leading versus trailing}
timeline_x <-read.csv("Data/FC_Seoul_2025_Time_Distribution.csv") |> # Cleans the dataset by shows time leading and trailing relative to 90 mins along with shot division and difference betwen their time leading versus trailing
  mutate(trailing_prop = Trailing/90) |>
  mutate(leading_prop = Leading/90) |>
  mutate(shots_division = shots_inside/shots) |>
  mutate(diff = Leading - Trailing)

fit = glm((shots_inside/shots) ~ (diff), data = timeline_x, family = binomial, weights = shots) #our model for these variables using a GLM with a weight on the amount of shots
summary(fit)

#xtable( summary(fit)$coef, digits = 4 ) prints the table in laTex

#pdf( "Leading.pdf", height = 5, width = 8 ) turns graph into a PDF

ggplot(aes(x= diff, y = shots_division),data = timeline_x) + # Graphs the difference as an scatterplot
  geom_point()+
  stat_smooth(method = "glm", #adds a line for the glm 
              method.args = list(family = "binomial"))+
  labs( y ="Proportion of shots inside",
       x = "Time leading in minutes")
#dev.off() 
```

## Objective 4

```{r, age graph and model}
age = read.csv( "Data/ages.csv" ) #Reads in the age dataset

t = table(age$Player) #Creates a player of every players age
p = names(t)[ t >= 3 ] # Keeps the ones where t is greater or equal to 3
age$saved = age$faced - age$goals_allowed # creates amount go goals goalkeeper saved
age$per_saved = age$saved/age$faced # Creates proportion of the amount of shots saved

fit = glmer( saved/faced ~ 1 + age + ( 1 | Player), 
             family = binomial, weights = faced, data = subset( age, Player %in% p ) ) # Creates our needed model subseted by the players from group p with us studying save proportion against age and factored by player
summary(fit)

#pdf( "age.pdf", height = 5, width = 8) pdf of the graph
ggplot(aes(x = age, y = per_saved, group = Player, color = Player), data = subset( age, Player %in% p ))+
  geom_point()+ #Creates a scatterplot with age, perportion saved, with player being by color
  geom_line()+ # Makes a line for each individual 
  theme_minimal()+ 
  labs(x = "Age",
       y="Proportion saved"
       ) 
#dev.off() turns off the pdf.
```
